## The "Validate StackBlitz URLs" Change

There was a specific documentation improvement in the Lexical project to validate StackBlitz URLs. The change "Validate stackblitz URLs in documentation (#6215)" was made by Bob Ippolito in the lexical-website package.

## What StackBlitz URLs Are Used For

Lexical hosts official live example code on StackBlitz, allowing developers to try out examples directly in the browser. StackBlitz URLs follow the pattern `stackblitz.com/github/facebook/lexical/tree/main/examples/[example-name]`. Some of the official examples include:

- Lexical React Plain Text — official live example code, created by Facebook on StackBlitz.
- Lexical React Rich — official live example code, created by Facebook on StackBlitz.
- Lexical Vanilla Js — official live example code, created by Facebook on StackBlitz.
- Lexical Tree View Plugin — official live example code, created by Facebook on StackBlitz.
- Lexical Website Toolbar — official live example code, created by Facebook on StackBlitz.

## Purpose of the Validation

The PR (#6215) added a test/check to validate that the StackBlitz URLs referenced in Lexical's documentation actually point to valid, existing example directories under `facebook/lexical/tree/main/examples`. This helps ensure that links in the documentation don't break as examples are added, renamed, or removed.

For contributors working with the repo, Lexical provides standard tooling to run checks: install dependencies with `pnpm install`, run unit tests with `pnpm run test-unit`, run e2e tests with `pnpm run test-e2e-chromium`, and lint/type check with `pnpm run ci-check`.

If you'd like, I can look at the specific implementation of PR #6215 to see exactly how the URL validation test was written. Just let me know.
